newsitem.title: USA: CME feeder cattle gains pared after new highs set.
newsitem.headline: CME feeder cattle gains pared after new highs set.

text.p: CME feeder cattle futures ran up early and set a new contract high in August before profit taking pared best levels at midsession, traders said. Live cattle futures ranged mixed at midsession with nearbys under pressure from cash concerns, traders said.

At 1109 CDT, feeder cattle stood 0.275 to 0.750 cent per lb higher with August up 0.350 at 81.300 cents after setting a new contract high early of 81.825 cents. Live cattle ranged from 0.200 cent lower to 0.400 higher with August off most at 63.725 cents.

Traders cited another decline in corn futures and the continued advance in the CME feeder cattle index for the early runup in feeders to a new high. Buy stops added to the early advance before profit taking pared gains, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.20 to $80.87 per cwt, the highest level since April 18, 1994.
Refco, Rosenthal Collins and ADM Investor Services notably bought August feeders while R.J. O'Brien sold, pit sources said.
Concern over slack packer demand for cash cattle and lower boxed beef values late last week weighed on live cattle futures. A break in pork complex futures also weighed on sentiment, traders said.

Packers were only lightly bidding $62 per cwt for cash cattle early Monday. The bids were down $1 from sales reported last week. Expectations are for demand to wane for steak items now that the two major U.S. cookout holidays, Memorial Day and Independence Day, have passed, they said.
R.J. O'Brien was a net buyer in August and also bought October while Cargill Investor Services sold both months. Rosenthal Collins bought August early, pit sources said.

Boneless beef futures rose early on commission house short covering with trimmings following in thin trade, traders said. E.D.&F. Man and ADM Investor Services bought August boneless while Lind-Waldock and turned sold an the days high of 96.00 cents per lb, traders said.

Lightly traded deferred boneless beef contracts posted new contract highs and both August and February trimmings set new highs on the early advance. Boneless beef was up 1.50 cents to unchanged with August up 0.70 at 95.20 cents. Trimmings were up 0.40 to unchanged with August up 0.40 at 44.50 cents.
